sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: 6.1 Perimeter Do you remember what the perimeter of a closed plane figure is?
sections.source_evidence: 6.1 Perimeter Do you remember what the perimeter of a closed plane figure is?

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: The perimeter of any closed plane figure is the distance covered along its boundary when you go around it once.
sections.source_evidence: The perimeter of any closed plane figure is the distance covered along its boundary when you go around it once.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: For a polygon, i.e., a closed plane figure made up of line segments, the perimeter is simply the sum of the lengths of its all sides, i.e., the total distance along its outer boundary.
sections.source_evidence: For a polygon, i.e., a closed plane figure made up of line segments, the perimeter is simply the sum of the lengths of its all sides, i.e., the total distance along its outer boundary.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: The perimeter of a polygon = the sum of the lengths of its all sides.
sections.source_evidence: The perimeter of a polygon = the sum of the lengths of its all sides.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: Let us revise the formulas for the perimeter of rectangles, squares, and triangles.
sections.source_evidence: Let us revise the formulas for the perimeter of rectangles, squares, and triangles.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: Perimeter of a rectangle Consider a rectangle ABCD whose length and breadth are 12 cm and 8 cm, respectively.
sections.source_evidence: Perimeter of a rectangle Consider a rectangle ABCD whose length and breadth are 12 cm and 8 cm, respectively.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: Perimeter of the rectangle = Sum of the lengths of its four sides = AB + BC + CD + DA A 12 cm B 8 cm D C PERIMETER AND AREA 6
sections.source_evidence: Perimeter of the rectangle = Sum of the lengths of its four sides = AB + BC + CD + DA A 12 cm B 8 cm D C PERIMETER AND AREA 6

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Ganita Prakash | Grade 6 130 = AB + BC + AB + BC = 2 × AB + 2 × BC = 2 × (AB + BC) = 2 × (12 cm + 8 cm) = 2 × (20 cm) = 40 cm.
sections.source_evidence: Ganita Prakash | Grade 6 130 = AB + BC + AB + BC = 2 × AB + 2 × BC = 2 × (AB + BC) = 2 × (12 cm + 8 cm) = 2 × (20 cm) = 40 cm.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: From this example, we see that — Perimeter of a rectangle = length + breadth + length + breadth.
sections.source_evidence: From this example, we see that — Perimeter of a rectangle = length + breadth + length + breadth.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth). The perimeter of a rectangle is twice the sum of its length and breadth.
sections.source_evidence: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth). The perimeter of a rectangle is twice the sum of its length and breadth.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: Perimeter of a square Debojeet wants to put coloured tape all around a square photo frame of side 1m as shown.
sections.source_evidence: Perimeter of a square Debojeet wants to put coloured tape all around a square photo frame of side 1m as shown.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: What will be the length of the coloured tape he requires?
sections.source_evidence: What will be the length of the coloured tape he requires?

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: Since Debojeet wants to put the coloured tape all around the square photo frame, he needs to find the perimeter of the photo frame.
sections.source_evidence: Since Debojeet wants to put the coloured tape all around the square photo frame, he needs to find the perimeter of the photo frame.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Thus, the length of the tape required = perimeter of the square = sum of the lengths of all four sides of the square = 1 m + 1 m + 1 m + 1 m = 4 m.
sections.source_evidence: Thus, the length of the tape required = perimeter of the square = sum of the lengths of all four sides of the square = 1 m + 1 m + 1 m + 1 m = 4 m.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: Now, we know that all four sides of a square are equal in length.
sections.source_evidence: Now, we know that all four sides of a square are equal in length.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: Therefore, in place of adding the lengths of each side, we can simply multiply the length of one side by 4. Thus, the length of the tape required = 4 × 1 m = 4 m.
sections.source_evidence: Therefore, in place of adding the lengths of each side, we can simply multiply the length of one side by 4. Thus, the length of the tape required = 4 × 1 m = 4 m.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: From this example, we see that Perimeter of a square = 4 × length of a side.
sections.source_evidence: From this example, we see that Perimeter of a square = 4 × length of a side.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: The perimeter of a square is quadruple the length of its side.
sections.source_evidence: The perimeter of a square is quadruple the length of its side.

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: Opposite sides of a rectangle are always equal.
sections.source_evidence: Opposite sides of a rectangle are always equal.
